class.name: NetwPredictIsland
class.brief_description: The local prediction boundary one entity declares: who it simulates alongside itself, and how that group is compared.
class.description: An entity predicts its own body under its own commands. An island widens that to the bodies whose motion its own motion depends on, so a divergence caused by a neighbour is a divergence the owner can see coming rather than one authority reports afterwards. An island is declared when it has members or a producer. Comparison and reconciliation settings alone do not set [member declared]. [codeblock] var island := NetwEntity.of(self).prediction.island island.from_interest() island.simulate_nearest(1) [/codeblock] The roster is read-only from outside. [member participants] returns a fresh copy and the verbs below are the only way in, because the engine resolves a slot's configuration from the roster and a member appended behind its back would leave that configuration describing a group the entity no longer has. [b]Explicit membership is exact, production is approximate.[/b] A roster the game wrote is a fact both peers hold, so it admits the fingerprint compare. A roster produced from interest is this peer's own resolution of its own scope, which the other peer never agreed to, so [method from_interest] declares [member approximate] itself and [member exact_claim] is rejected on it. Reached through [member NetwPredictionHandle.island], which is never [code]null[/code].

method.name: add
method.description: Adds [param entity] as an explicit member, once. Every verb that names a member calls this first, so membership and what is declared about it can never disagree. Rejected across a scene boundary: an island is a group one solve steps together, and two scenes are two worlds. An island bound to no owner has no scene to cross and admits anything.

method.name: bind_owner
method.description: Binds the entity this rule belongs to, which is what [method add]'s scene-boundary check reads. Weakly held, because the entity owns the handle that owns this. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: duplicate_rule
method.description: A detached copy carrying every declaration this rule holds. The two comparison claims are copied through their setters last, so the copy resolves the same invariant the original did rather than landing on a half-set pair.

method.name: fidelity_of
method.description: The [enum NetwPredict.Fidelity] declared for [param entity], or [code]-1[/code] when the island declared none and the member is decided by [member promotion]. A member the island does not have returns [code]-1[/code] too, because it has declared nothing either way.

method.name: from_interest
method.description: Produces members from the entity's resolved interest scope, or from [param layer] when one is named. Naming the same layer twice declares it once. Production is what makes an island approximate, so this sets [member approximate] itself, and it is rejected on an island that already claimed exact comparison.

method.name: has_member
method.description: Whether [param entity] is on this island's explicit roster. Ask this rather than searching [member participants], which returns a copy.

method.name: inheritable
method.description: A copy marked [member inherited], for handing this scene's rule to one descendant entity, or [code]null[/code] when the rule names nobody. Null rather than an empty rule, because a rule that only set a tolerance says nothing about who is being compared and must not opt a descendant into a compare it never asked for.

method.name: observe
method.description: Adds [param entity] and keeps it a displayed proxy, exempt from whatever [member promotion] would otherwise decide for it.

method.name: predict_commands
method.description: Adds [param entity] and installs [param predictor] as its substituted command producer, called as [code](participant, tick)[/code] and returning an input [Dictionary]. A simulated member without one runs the zero-input COAST policy.

method.name: predictor_of
method.description: The substituted command producer declared for [param entity], or an invalid [Callable] when it declared none.

method.name: remove
method.description: Removes [param entity] and everything declared about it. A fidelity or a predictor cannot outlive the member it was declared for, because the next member added would inherit it.

method.name: set_fidelity
method.description: Declares [param entity]'s [enum NetwPredict.Fidelity] without adding it. For a member the island does not have this stores nothing, which is what separates it from [method simulate] and [method observe]: those two name a member, this one only describes one.

method.name: simulate
method.description: Adds [param entity] and promotes it for local simulation. A valid [param predict_commands] is installed as that member's command producer in the same act.

method.name: simulate_all
method.description: Promotes every produced member for local simulation.

method.name: simulate_nearest
method.description: Promotes the nearest [param count] produced members for local simulation. A negative budget promotes none rather than being rejected, so a computed count can be handed in without a guard.

method.name: simulate_within
method.description: Promotes produced members within [param meters] for local simulation. A negative radius promotes none, for the same reason [method simulate_nearest] clamps.

method.name: watch_declaration
method.description: Installs the callback every act that MOVES this declaration invokes, so the pool's own columns can be restated rather than re-read on every drive. Reading a member never invokes it, and neither does a promotion policy, which decides who is stepped rather than what a drive is judged against. [method duplicate_rule] and [method inheritable] hand back a copy with NO callback, because a copy belongs to the entity that takes it and announcing the original's declaration through it would restate the wrong slot. [b]Server Only.[/b]

members.member: Whether this island is compared by tolerance rather than by exact fingerprint. Setting it clears [member exact_claim]: the two are the same question asked twice and may not disagree.

Whether this island claims a roster at all, and therefore whether the entity is admitted to the fingerprint compare. Derived from whether the island has members or a producer. Other settings do not declare the island.

Whether this island claims its roster is a fact both peers hold, which is what admits exact comparison. Setting it clears [member approximate]. A produced island cannot claim it, and the write is rejected rather than stored: the claim would not be a fact about this island, it would be a statement the roster itself contradicts.

Whether this rule came from the containing scene rather than from the entity's own declaration. An inherited rule is re-inherited on reparent. The entity's first own declaration replaces an inherited rule whole rather than refining it, and naming a member or a producer is the only act that counts as one. A tolerance or a reconcile mode written onto an inherited rule refines the scene's rule, which is what a game that wrote only those asked for.

Ticks a [constant NetwPredict.PACING_DELAY_CLOSED] group holds each command before the transition it labels opens. Clamped at zero, since a negative hold is a command scheduled before it was authored.
When this island's members open transitions, as a [enum NetwPredict.Pacing]. The group owns the mechanism a pacing names, so this selects one rather than performing it.

The entities explicitly named as members, through [method add] and the verbs that call it. A fresh copy per read. Editing it changes nothing, because the engine resolves a slot's configuration from the roster and a member appended behind the verbs would leave that configuration describing a group the entity no longer has.
The interest layers this island's membership is produced from, [code]&""[/code] meaning the entity's own resolved scope. Declared through [method from_interest].
Which produced members are promoted to local simulation, as a [enum NetwPredict.Promotion]. Explicit promotion through [method simulate] is not a policy and is unaffected: it names one member.
The structural budget of [constant NetwPredict.PROMOTION_NEAREST], in members.
The radius of [constant NetwPredict.PROMOTION_WITHIN], in metres.

How divergence is reconciled across the island, as a [enum NetwPredict.Reconcile]. Under [constant NetwPredict.RECONCILE_JOINT], the group restores and replays its members together when a basis arrives. The engine may reject joint reconciliation when a member cannot replay at the required tier. A joint pass spans EVERY member in one act and opens no per-member correction episode of its own, so a member's episode books record what its own independent corrections did and never what the group did on its behalf. The group's own evidence is the joint counters on [NetwPredictStats] instead, and reading a member's episode as if it covered the group would report a group that never corrected.
